method: Allegedly signed out two tablets of a controlled substance from a resident's prescription supply after the resident had been discharged and transferred to another unit; documentation indicated the medication was administered, but the resident did not receive it, and the tablets were later found missing from inventory.
status: Arrested on one count of Obtaining Drugs by Fraud, a Class D felony.

title: Registered nurse stole fentanyl vials at work and altered medication logs to conceal theft
method: Stole 255 vials of fentanyl 100 mcg/2 mL and altered medication logs attempting to conceal the theft; tested positive for fentanyl on a for-cause drug screen at work; pleaded guilty and was convicted in federal court of felony acquiring or obtaining possession of a controlled substance by misrepresentation, fraud, forgery, deception or subterfuge.
status: License placed on 36-month probation; terms include no access to narcotics or controlled substances; Board order.

title: Hospital lead pharmacy technician diverted Oxycodone by substituting Fludrocortisone during prepackaging for automated dispensing system
setting: a hospital in Prince George's County, Maryland
method: Switched Oxycodone 5 mg tablets with Fludrocortisone 0.1 mg tablets during prepackaging to refill an automated medication dispensing system and entered zero-count refills to conceal the swap; admitted to personally ingesting the Oxycodone.
status: Registration revoked.

title: Pharmacy technician diverted alprazolam, zolpidem and other controlled substances from a national pharmacy chain in Easton, Maryland, by taking pills from bottles
setting: a national pharmacy chain, at two stores in Easton, Maryland
drug: Alprazolam (Xanax), zolpidem (Ambien), carisoprodol (Soma), diazepam, eszopiclone (Lunesta), and clonazepam
method: Stole controlled substances from the pharmacy's stores by taking them from pill bottles; was seen consuming alprazolam tablets and placing additional tablets in a lab coat pocket; admitted stealing multiple controlled substances.
status: Final order of revocation of pharmacy technician registration; registration revoked.

title: Unlicensed Director of Nursing at Cherrydale Post Acute charged with stealing oxycodone from a person
method: Allegedly stole a quantity of oxycodone, a Schedule II controlled substance, from another person with intent to permanently deprive that person of the medication while employed at Cherrydale Post Acute.
status: Arrested and charged with one count of Theft of a Controlled Substance, first offense, and two counts of Unlicensed Practice as Registered Nurse or Practical Nurse; booked into the Greenville County Detention Center. Presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

title: ER charge nurse self-reported diverting medication wastes for personal use at Ascension St. Vincent Anderson
method: self-reported diverting medication wastes for personal use; terminated for violating the drug policy
status: self-reported to PLA; terminated; enrolled in IPRP in August 2025 and signed a 3-year RMA; board recommended renewal on probation for the length of the RMA, with CEUs and referral of pending criminal charges to the OAG

title: Nurse charged with obtaining a controlled substance by fraud or deceit and wasting narcotics at Community North
method: charged with obtaining a controlled substance by fraud or deceit; diversion was suspended due to wasting of narcotics at work; positive drug test for marijuana
status: entered a diversion program that was completed and charges dismissed and expunged in October 2025; self-reported to ISNAP and entered a monitoring agreement; board recommended renewal free and clear

title: Hospital nurse found with Dilaudid and Hydrocodone waste in pocket from work
method: charged with possession of a narcotic drug and public intoxication; pled guilty to possession of a narcotic drug; had waste in pocket from work consisting of a Dilaudid pill and a Hydrocodone pill; terminated from Methodist Hospital
status: pled guilty in January 2025; completed probation in January 2026; terminated in August 2024; was unsuccessfully discharged from ISNAP in July 2025; board recommended renewal on indefinite probation, reengagement with ISNAP, a 3- to 5-year RMA, and CEUs

title: Rehabilitation center nurse accused of stealing patients' painkillers and drug logs
setting: a rehabilitation center in Sandy, Utah
method: Alleged to have stolen medications and drug logs from patients at the rehabilitation center where the nurse worked; police stated the nurse admitted to taking medications over the previous two months, allegedly taking drugs from patients who had multiple packs knowing they would not notice they were missing.
status: Arrested and booked into the Salt Lake County Jail; charged with one felony count of pattern of unlawful activity and several misdemeanors including theft and intentional abuse or neglect of a vulnerable adult.

title: Registered nurse removed fentanyl from medication safe without order or documentation and failed to document controlled substance administration/wasting; license revoked
setting: Grants Pass Surgery Center, Hearthstone Nursing and Rehabilitation Center, Bay Area Hospital
drug: fentanyl, oxycodone, hydromorphone, alprazolam, lorazepam, tramadol
method: removed fentanyl from a medication safe without a written order or documentation; failed to document administration or wasting of controlled substances; wasted oxycodone without allowing a witness to verify the medication; delayed wasting of controlled substances
status: Registered nurse license revoked

title: Hospital nurse accused of stealing opioids from patients at Grand Strand Medical Center
method: Allegedly stole opioid drugs on six separate occasions while working at the hospital, under the guise of providing them to patients, and then either failed to document taking them or fraudulently documented them as administered to a patient.
status: Arrested on several charges of theft of controlled substances and violating drug distribution law; released after posting $12,000 bail.

title: Licensed practical nurse charged with stealing oxycodone from resident at Simpsonville Post Acute
method: Allegedly knowingly and intentionally took a quantity of Oxycodone belonging to a resident and diverted Oxycodone prescribed to the resident for personal use.
status: Arrested and charged with one count of Theft of a Controlled Substance, 1st Offense; booked into Greenville County Detention Center; prosecution by the South Carolina Attorney General's Office.

title: Registered nurse admitted obtaining and consuming oxycodone without a prescription and had controlled-substance administration and documentation errors involving two patients; voluntarily surrendered license
method: Admitted obtaining and consuming oxycodone without a prescription; employer reported controlled-substance administration and documentation errors for two patients, and the licensee could not account for what medications were administered or why documentation was made; also admitted administering medication to a patient without a provider order and later admitted obtaining and consuming two oxycodone pills.
status: Voluntary surrender of registered nurse license accepted; may apply for reinstatement after a minimum of three years.

title: Registered nurse obtained Vyvanse from workplace without authorization and self-administered
setting: Their workplace (as stated in the source)
method: obtained a generic equivalent to Vyvanse from their workplace without a medical order and without authorization; took it home and administered it to themselves
status: registered nurse license placed on 36-month probation; admitted allegations

title: Registered nurse alleged to have obtained controlled substances from a Texas pharmacy using unauthorized prescriptions and co-worker prescriber numbers
drug: Zolpidem Tartrate, Eszopiclone, Acetaminophen-Codeine #3, Guaifenesin-Codeine, Butalbital-Acetaminophen-Caffeine, and Hydrocodone
method: Alleged to have obtained these medications from a pharmacy in Texas, for themself and a family member, through the use of unauthorized electronically communicated prescriptions, using the names and Drug Enforcement Administration numbers of three co-worker prescribers.
status: Stipulated Order for Probation; license placed on probation, with a 24-month period of probation to begin upon return to supervised nursing practice. Any monitored practice completed in Texas in compliance with the Texas Board of Nursing order counts toward the 24 months.

title: Licensed practical nurse found to have ingested prescription medications and possessed Adavan at Delaware Hospital for the Chronically Ill
setting: Delaware Hospital for the Chronically Ill
method: ingested several prescription medications without telling her supervisor; was found with Adavan in her pocket that should have been administered to a patient but was claimed missing; Hearing Officer found a pattern of theft and consumption of controlled substances
status: Board suspended the license for five years, required monthly random drug screens, and required 12 CEs (6 in ethics, 6 in substance abuse)

title: Sweetbriar Assisted Living nurse sentenced for hydrocodone theft and falsifying records
method: obtaining hydrocodone by fraud; admitted stealing hydrocodone intended for patients for personal use and falsifying records to cover up the theft
status: sentenced to five years of probation; previously pleaded guilty

title: Former Trinity Home Health/Hospice nurses accused of diluting and diverting patients' morphine and hydromorphone
drug: morphine and hydromorphone; prescription pain medication
method: Allegedly diluted nursing home patients' medications; administered morphine instead of hydromorphone; brought unused medication back to the office after a patient died and ingested it; investigation found multiple instances of drug diversion.
status: Charges across suspects include Endangering a Vulnerable Adult (B felony), Conspiracy (C felony), and Theft of Property (C felony); two former nurses voluntarily surrendered their nursing licenses after admitting to the drug-diversion allegations; arrest warrants were issued.

title: Hospital nurse diverted hydrocodone intended for a patient and falsified records
method: Admitted to taking two 5 mg hydrocodone pills intended for a patient, keeping them for personal use, and falsely documenting in the patient file that the medication had been given to the patient.
status: Pleaded guilty to obtaining a controlled substance by misrepresentation, fraud, forgery, deception, and subterfuge; terminated from employment on June 27, 2015; faces up to four years in federal prison; sentencing set for October 1, 2018.

title: Nevada nursing board found a licensed practical nurse withdrew morphine from patient dispensers at a rural hospital without documenting it
setting: a rural hospital and nursing home in Caliente, Nevada
method: withdrew morphine from the medication dispensers of two patients without documenting what happened to the controlled substance
status: license stripped; barred from reapplying for five years

title: Emergency room nurse suspended indefinitely for diverting controlled substances from an automated medication administration machine
method: repeatedly withdrew controlled substances from an automated medication administration machine and failed to document that they were administered to patients; a drug screen showed three controlled substances in the nurse's system
status: suspended until able to demonstrate twelve months of continued sobriety and thereafter placed on probation; the Georgia Board of Nursing's proposed sanction was upheld

title: Registered nurse reprimanded for misappropriating narcotics from employer for personal use
method: intentional misappropriation of various narcotics from employer for personal use
status: Consent Agreement; public reprimand

title: Three former Trinity Hospital hospice nurses accused of stealing drugs and endangering patients
setting: Trinity Hospital's Home Health and Hospice program
drug: morphine and hydromorphine; drugs prescribed for hospice patients
method: Accused of stealing drugs prescribed for hospice patients; two charged with endangering a patient by diluting medication or giving morphine instead of prescribed hydromorphine; alleged conspiracy to steal drugs; one allegedly confessed to ingesting unused medication and self-administering for over a year; investigation found multiple drug diversions in records of 104 patients.
status: Charged with felony offenses; two voluntarily surrendered nursing licenses after admitting to board allegations; one arrested and signed promise to appear.

title: Health system settles alleged opioid diversion case over tens of thousands of missing oxycodone 30 mg tablets
method: Alleged large-scale diversion of opioids; tens of thousands of oxycodone 30 mg tablets were reported missing over more than four years, and the health system allegedly failed to notify authorities of the suspected diversion within the time required by federal law.
status: Agreed to pay $4.1 million to settle the claims; the system said it has since overhauled pharmacy recordkeeping and reporting and implemented electronic inventory systems. At the time, the largest settlement of its kind for hospital drug diversion; the DEA investigation was launched in 2017.

title: Georgia hospital settles allegations over unaccounted 30 mg oxycodone tablets believed diverted
method: allegedly failed to provide effective controls and procedures to guard against theft and loss of controlled substances, resulting in tens of thousands of 30 mg oxycodone tablets unaccounted for and believed diverted for illegal uses over a four-year period, and allegedly failed to notify DEA of suspected diversion within the requisite time period
status: $4.1 million civil settlement and performance improvement plan with DEA

title: Hospital pharmacy technician diverted hydrocodone and oxycodone from a pharmacy vault through fraudulent automated dispensing transactions
drug: hydrocodone and oxycodone (Schedule II controlled substances)
method: Stole 8,505 pills, each containing 5 milligrams of either hydrocodone or oxycodone, from the hospital's pharmacy vault between February 2017 and March 2018, using her authorized fingerprint and unique login to conduct 82 fraudulent transactions in the hospital's new automated medication distribution and tracking system, which she found did not require a valid prescription to dispense medication to patients being discharged; gave the pills to her boyfriend for his personal use and used some herself.
status: Sentenced to 12 months in jail plus six years of court supervision; pleaded guilty in June to one count each of possessing with intent to distribute hydrocodone and oxycodone; had repaid $1,033 to the hospital before sentencing.

title: Hilo clinic physician and employees accused of unlawfully distributing opioids
method: accused of prescribing and unlawfully distributing powerful narcotics, sedatives and opioids such as hydrocodone, oxycodone, fentanyl and morphine
status: arrested; scheduled to stand trial in U.S. District Court in June

title: Las Vegas nurse sentenced for illegally prescribing hydrocodone and oxycodone in a cash-for-prescriptions scheme
method: Alleged and admitted conduct: arranged with a surgical technician and a physician to give hydrocodone and oxycodone to patients without a legitimate medical purpose in exchange for cash, and wrote illegal prescriptions without a medical purpose; also billed Medicare and Medicaid for prescriptions for lidocaine, modafinil and diclofenac sodium without having examined the patient.
status: Pleaded guilty to eight counts of distribution of a controlled substance and eight counts of health care fraud; sentenced to more than six years in federal prison, three years of supervised release, and ordered to pay $3,749,121 in restitution.

title: Pharmacist stole Schedule IV controlled substances from Institutional Care Pharmacy
drug: zolpidem, modafinil, clonazepam, tramadol, lorazepam, alprazolam
method: stole controlled substances from employer; observed on security camera; admitted stealing; retrieved stolen drugs from purse and residence
status: license suspended indefinitely; summary suspension removed

title: Rawlins physician sentenced federally for dispensing medically unnecessary controlled substances
drug: oxycodone, alprazolam, hydrocodone, tramadol and other controlled substances
method: Pleaded guilty to 20 counts of dispensing medically unnecessary controlled substances; prosecutors said some patients were addicts or became addicted, that drugs were traded for sexual favors, and that 430 oxycodone pills were prescribed to a young female patient in return for lewd photographs.
status: Sentenced to 20 concurrent five-year prison terms, six years of supervised release, a $2,000 special assessment and $400 restitution; license previously suspended by the state medical board.

title: Nursing home licensed practical nurse convicted of diverting 638 narcotics pills from residents
setting: Georgiana Health and Rehabilitation. Also referred to as Butler County Nursing Home in the Attorney General's release title.
method: Diverted 638 narcotics pills, including hydrocodone, oxycodone, tramadol and lorazepam, from nursing home residents for whom the medications were intended; thefts occurred between November 5, 2020, and January 19, 2021.
status: Pleaded guilty to four counts of second-degree theft of property; sentencing set for July 7; faces one to 10 years imprisonment and up to a $15,000 fine for each conviction.

title: Emergency room nurse sentenced to probation for diverting fentanyl from a Lincoln hospital pharmacy
method: Checked out fentanyl from the hospital pharmacy more than 200 times between May and June 2022; 55 discrepancies were found; 2.65 mg of fentanyl was unaccounted for; in some cases checked out fentanyl without a doctor's order and in others reported administering it within five minutes of patient discharge; denied stealing or using the drug but urine tested positive for fentanyl.
status: Pleaded guilty to acquiring a controlled substance by fraud; sentenced to three years of probation; gave up nursing license.

title: Surgical practice nurse sentenced for tampering with fentanyl, morphine, and meperidine and replacing them with saline
method: extracted medication from vials of fentanyl, morphine, and meperidine and replaced it with saline, compromising at least 78 vials, including those intended for surgical patients; testing found compromised vials contained less than 15% of the actual medication and that tampering rendered multiple vials unsterile
status: sentenced to 48 months in prison and three years of supervised release; pleaded guilty to the charges; plea agreement requires permanent surrender of the nursing license

title: Registered nurse convicted of tampering with fentanyl citrate vials and obtaining controlled substance by fraud at Chamberlain hospital
setting: a hospital in Chamberlain, South Dakota
method: Tampered with a vial of fentanyl citrate for injection by removing the fentanyl and replacing the majority of it with saline solution, then returned the tampered vial to storage knowing the diluted fentanyl could be dispensed to surgical patients; also obtaining a controlled substance by misrepresentation, fraud, forgery, deception, and subterfuge.
status: Convicted and sentenced to two years of probation and a $100 special assessment to the Federal Crime Victims Fund.

title: ICU nurse sentenced for tampering with fentanyl and hydromorphone at Ardmore hospital
setting: Mercy Hospital Intensive Care Unit, Ardmore, Oklahoma
method: stole fentanyl and hydromorphone intended for intensive care patients; removed the pain medication from vials, refilled the empty vials with tap water, and returned the tampered vials to the controlled storage locker; admitted the conduct
status: sentenced to 12 months in prison for one count of Tampering with Consumer Products; pleaded guilty on August 31, 2023

title: WakeMed nurse charged with stealing fentanyl from IV bag
method: Allegedly had access to the drug through the job and stole 2,500 mL of fentanyl from an IV bag on Oct. 19.
status: Charged with two felony counts: embezzling/diverting a controlled substance by registrant/employee and obtaining possession of a controlled substance by fraud/forgery; arrested Oct. 30; out on bond; next court date Nov. 19; no longer employed by WakeMed.

title: Birmingham-area nursing home nurse diverted hydrocodone tablets; pleaded guilty to theft
method: The nurse, responsible for distributing medication to residents, stole opioid tablets from the nursing home. A nurse discovered missing hydrocodone in July 2024, and an investigation found discrepancies involving over 100 hydrocodone tablets over approximately two months. The nurse was terminated by the facility after the missing hydrocodone was discovered.
status: Pled guilty to Theft of Property in the Second Degree, a Class C felony; received a 15-month suspended sentence.

title: Hospital pharmacist diverted ketamine and falsified destruction records at Mercy Hospital Anderson Pharmacy
drug: ketamine, a Schedule III controlled substance
method: The Board found the pharmacist stole ketamine from his employer pharmacy over about six months, sold two bottles for $100 each, provided ketamine to a drug dealer, and falsified drug destruction records by showing a vial to a witness, having the required form signed, then leaving without destroying the drugs.
status: Permanently revoked the pharmacist license; removed the summary suspension order.

title: Muncie hospital pharmacy license put on probation after pharmacy manager diverted opioids using unused transaction types
method: The attorney general's administrative complaint alleged the hospital failed over a 44-month period to maintain effective controls against theft and diversion of controlled substances, allowing a pharmacy manager to repeatedly remove Schedule II narcotics through normally-unused transaction types while disguising the withdrawals as legitimate transfers to two outpatient clinics. Investigators said the reported losses included more than 32,000 milliliters of hydromorphone, more than 3,300 milliliters of methadone solution, more than 4,000 methadone tablets and smaller amounts of morphine, with the hospital estimating its loss at more than $121,000.
status: The Indiana Board of Pharmacy voted 3-2 to accept a revised settlement placing the hospital's pharmacy license and controlled substance registration on indefinite probation for at least three years, imposing the maximum $44,000 civil fine plus a $5 statutory fee, and requiring quarterly independent audits, two unannounced compliance inspections, a drug diversion certificate program for pharmacy leadership and additional diversion-prevention continuing education. Also reported: The hospital's pharmacy license and controlled substances registration were placed on indefinite probation for not less than three years, with quarterly outside audits for the first two years, two unannounced compliance inspections, required diversion-prevention training for pharmacy leadership, and a $44,000 fine; the hospital reported the loss to the DEA and Board in July 2024 and filed an amended DEA Form 106 in November 2024, and in August 2025 the county prosecutor's office filed charges against the pharmacist.

title: Registered nurse accused of diverting morphine from OrthoNebraska surgical unit
method: Alleged entering fictitious orders in patient charts to divert morphine for himself; admitted diverting morphine by adding or changing the ordered amount, charting the difference, or charting medical 'waste'; accessed automated medication dispensing machine, sometimes using co-workers' login information.
status: Booked on seven felony counts of intentionally violating a narcotic drug law; placed on leave then later fired; scheduled court appearance. Nebraska nursing license was listed as active until Oct. 31, 2026, as of the report, with no disciplinary information shown.

title: Edmond hospital employee charged with stealing fentanyl waste from OU Health
method: Accused of diverting fentanyl waste: a hospital report flagged more than 15 transactions involving fentanyl waste, including 'override cancel' or 'remove cancel' with fentanyl 100 mcg/2ml fifteen times; surveillance video reportedly showed the employee blocking the camera's view, removing vials from a drawer and putting them in his pocket, and using a syringe and needle to take leftover waste from drip bags for personal use. Police said the employee later admitted to the theft of fentanyl waste, totaling about $430.
status: Charged with larceny of controlled drugs

title: A pharmacy technician diverted narcotics by taking and selling them, and the pharmacy's controlled-substance records were found inaccurate as a result
method: A pharmacy technician took narcotics from the pharmacy and sold them; a subsequent state board order found the pharmacy had failed to maintain accurate records of the receipt and disposal of hydrocodone and alprazolam over an extended period.
status: The technician was terminated and the technician's license was revoked by the state pharmacy board; the pharmacy itself was placed on two years' probation, fined $5,000, and assessed investigation costs by that board. A separate state board later granted the pharmacy's out-of-state permit application subject to one year of probation because of these violations.

title: Pharmacy technician accused of removing pills from a filled Oxycontin prescription and returning it to conceal the theft
method: Alleged to have pulled a customer's filled prescription from the staging area, removed pills, and returned the prescription to the staging area; the customer later reported 198 of 270 pills missing
status: Registration summarily suspended pending a show cause hearing

title: Applicant for reinstatement granted probation after prior controlled substance diversion from pharmacy
method: diversion of a controlled substance from a pharmacy
status: Reinstatement granted with 3 years probation

title: Nurse at a medical center in Caliente investigated for unaccounted morphine; license revoked
setting: a medical center in Caliente, Nevada
method: investigated for two 2015 incidents involving unaccounted morphine; investigation indicated obtaining morphine syringes for patients but failing to document whether the drug was administered
status: Nevada State Board of Nursing revoked the nursing license for five years for unprofessional conduct

title: Pain clinic physician indicted for prescribing fentanyl, oxycodone and other controlled substances without patient examinations
method: Charged by indictment with unlawful distribution of controlled substances: allegedly prescribing fentanyl, oxycodone, methadone, morphine and other controlled substances on many occasions without patients actually being seen by the physician, and billing Medicare, Medicaid and the Bureau of Workers' Compensation for medically unnecessary prescriptions; also alleged to have received payments from a pharmaceutical company for sham speaking engagements about a fentanyl spray.
status: Federal grand jury indictment: 88 counts of unlawful distribution of a controlled substance, one count of unlawful distribution of a controlled substance with death resulting, eight counts of health care fraud and 17 counts of violating the anti-kickback law. Charges only; no finding or plea reported.

title: Physician charged with health care fraud and distributing Suboxone without medical necessity through a clinic
method: Charged in a federal indictment with a health care fraud scheme that involved marketing prescription creams in low-income neighborhoods and persistently mailing those creams to Medicaid customers, and with prescribing and distributing Suboxone without medical necessity.
status: Charged in a seven-count federal indictment on October 30, 2018; scheduled for an initial appearance in federal court.

title: Nurse practitioner forged physicians' signatures to issue unauthorized controlled-substance prescriptions at two Montgomery pill-mill practices
setting: Family Practice and Mercy Family Health Care, Montgomery medical practices
drug: fentanyl, hydrocodone, oxycodone, alprazolam, and methadone
method: Convicted at trial of issuing unnecessary and illegitimate prescriptions for controlled substances and, because she lacked authority as a nurse practitioner to refill Schedule II prescriptions without physician approval, forging physicians' signatures on those prescriptions; the unnecessary office visits and unlawful prescriptions were billed to insurers. Conduct spanned 2013 through 2016, initially at a Montgomery medical practice and later at a second practice she opened.
status: Convicted by federal jury on 17 counts of unlawful distribution of controlled substances, one count of conspiracy to distribute controlled substances, four counts of health care fraud, and one count of conspiracy to commit health care fraud; sentenced to 10 years and received enhancements for obstructing justice and abuse of trust.

title: Physician found guilty of operating a pill mill and prescribing opioids without legitimate medical purpose
method: prescribed opioids and other drugs without a legitimate medical purpose; operated a pill mill; aggravated trafficking in drugs; tampering with records; illegal processing of drug documents
status: Found guilty on 187 counts; sentencing scheduled for July 3, 2019

title: Anchorage nurse practitioner charged with manslaughter and drug distribution for opioid prescriptions without office visits
drug: diazepam, oxycodone, tramadol, hydrocodone, and Ambien
method: Alleged: used position as a nurse practitioner to fraudulently give a patient and others vast quantities of prescription opioids; routinely prescribed controlled substances to friends and acquaintances without office visits, chart notes, rationalization, or explanation, often via text or the internet; agreed to meet to write a prescription after a request for pain pills.
status: Indicted on 18 felony counts including manslaughter and criminally negligent homicide plus drug distribution counts; pleaded not guilty; license suspended by the Alaska Board of Nursing. An outside review found no justification for many of the prescriptions; the nursing board had previously suspended the practitioner's license.

title: Pain clinic physician pleaded guilty to operating a pill mill and selling oxycodone for kickbacks
method: operated a pill mill out of his practice for more than seven years and sold oxycodone in exchange for financial kickbacks; also staged a break-in at his practice to make a fraudulent insurance claim
status: pleaded guilty; sentenced to five years probation, ordered to pay a $5,000 fine, forfeit more than $524,000, and surrender his medical license and DEA registration

title: Physician pleads guilty to illegally prescribing opioids and falsifying records at a Lake Milton medical office
setting: a medical office in Lake Milton, Ohio
drug: opioids including oxycodone and hydrocodone, often in combination with benzodiazepines and stimulants
method: illegally prescribed controlled substances outside the usual course of professional practice and without a legitimate medical purpose; used false diagnoses, falsified patient pain intensity scales in medical charts, increased dosages, and prescribed for prolonged periods without evidence of efficacy; ignored urine drug screen results and warning signs of patient addiction and abuse; unlawfully prescribed opioids to two patients who later fatally overdosed and to an individual under the age of 21
status: pleaded guilty to illegally distributing controlled substances, causing the deaths of two patients, unlawfully distributing a controlled substance to a person under the age of 21, and health care fraud; sentencing scheduled for May 17, 2022

title: Mount Pleasant pharmacy technician charged with stealing OxyContin and Adderall from CVS pharmacy
setting: CVS Pharmacy on Ben Sawyer Boulevard
method: Allegedly stole tablets of OxyContin and Adderall from the pharmacy while working as a pharmacy technician.
status: Charged with two counts of theft of a controlled substance; booked into the Al Cannon Detention Center and later released on own recognizance.

title: Hospice nurse admitted diverting oxycodone and Oxycontin from two patients
method: The nurse picked up prescriptions for two hospice patients, signed for oxycodone and Oxycontin, delivered fewer tablets than she signed for, and set up e-prescribing requests without physician orders; she admitted to police that she diverted prescription medication from the patients.
status: The Board suspended the nurse's license for an indefinite period, stayed the suspension on compliance with treatment, monitoring, and practice restrictions, and restricted the nurse from working in settings with access to controlled substances.

title: Pain clinic nurse practitioner convicted of diverting opioids to a family member using other patients' names
setting: a pain management clinic (Eagle River Pain and Wellness)
method: wrote opioid prescriptions in the names of other individuals in order to divert nearly 5,000 pills to a live-in, opioid-addicted partner, and created false appointment records for those individuals to conceal the diversion; also pre-signed and pre-dated prescriptions for non-medical staff to distribute to patients for cash when out of the office
status: convicted by a federal jury on 10 felony counts, including distribution of a controlled substance resulting in death, distribution/dispensing of a controlled substance, and maintaining a drug-involved premises; per the U.S. Attorney's Office for the District of Alaska (Nov. 12, 2026), this jury conviction was later overturned because the presiding judge failed to recuse himself, and the defendant was resentenced after a guilty plea

title: Pharmacy technician took controlled substance from pharmacy for personal use
method: Took controlled substance from the pharmacy for personal use
status: Suspended until cleared by a mental health professional plus 5 years rehabilitation probation

title: Pharmacy technician admitted to theft of controlled substances from her employer; credential revoked
method: admitted to the theft of various controlled substances from her employer
status: credential revoked; prohibited from applying or reapplying to practice or assist in the practice of pharmacy

title: Pain clinic nurse practitioner conspired to dispense fentanyl by forging a physician's signature on prescriptions
method: Convicted of conspiring to prescribe fentanyl outside the usual course of professional practice and without a legitimate medical purpose; admitted to seeing patients without physician oversight while impaired by her own drug use, and to asking a co-defendant nurse practitioner to forge a physician's signature on controlled-substance prescriptions.
status: Sentenced to 20 months in federal prison after a 50% sentence reduction for cooperating in the prosecution of the clinic's co-owning physicians.

title: Pharmacy technician admitted to stealing controlled substances from employer pharmacy
method: Admitted to the theft of controlled substances from the employer pharmacy.
status: Credential revoked; prohibited from applying or reapplying to practice or assist in the practice of pharmacy.

title: Pharmacy technician accused of forging controlled substance prescriptions from employer pharmacy
method: Alleged to have forged controlled substance prescriptions from the employer pharmacy.
status: Credential revoked; prohibited from applying or reapplying to practice or assist in the practice of pharmacy.

title: Registrant's registration revoked for diversion of controlled substance from pharmacy
method: diversion of a controlled substance from a pharmacy
status: Revocation

title: Nursing home director of nursing used pre-signed prescription pads to divert hydrocodone
method: Used pre-signed prescription pads left by the facility's medical director to fax fraudulent prescriptions to the facility's pharmacy, then received and kept the narcotics from the pharmacy's courier instead of administering them
status: Pleaded guilty to Theft of Property Second Degree; sentenced to 18 months in community corrections and surrendered nursing license

title: National chain pharmacy manager disciplined after oxycodone reported lost/stolen as employee pilferage
drug: Oxycodone HCL 10 mg and 15 mg tablets
method: The pharmacy reported an occurrence classified as employee pilferage; a DEA report listed oxycodone HCL 10 mg and 15 mg tablets lost or stolen. The Board found the pharmacist violated patient safety and standard-of-care rules for filling questionable CII prescriptions without validation and for refusing-to-dispense requirements; fraud and false-record charges were dismissed as unsubstantiated.
status: Consent order: license reprimanded, placed on probation for at least one year, required continuing education, and a $1,000 fine.

title: Pharmacy technician's credential revoked for theft of controlled substances from employer pharmacy
method: theft of controlled substances from employer pharmacy
status: credential revoked; prohibited from applying or reapplying to practice or assist in the practice of pharmacy

title: VA nurse pleaded guilty to stealing fentanyl, morphine and hydromorphone
setting: Denver Veterans Affairs (VA) Medical Center, VA Eastern Colorado Health Care System
method: stealing fentanyl, morphine and hydromorphone from the Veterans Affairs Medical Center in Denver
status: Pleaded guilty; sentenced to 14 months in prison

title: VA pharmacy supervisor suspected of stealing painkillers and testosterone over five years
setting: George Wahlen Veterans Affairs (VA) Medical Center, VA Salt Lake City Health Care System
method: suspected of stealing more than 24,000 painkillers and 25 vials of testosterone over five years
status: Suspected; no disposition stated

title: Arkansas nurse self-reported diverting and consuming hydrocodone from employer
method: self-reported diverting and consuming hydrocodone from employer
status: Self-reported; no disciplinary action stated

title: Registered nurse sentenced to probation for stealing OxyContin from a hospital narcotics cabinet and replacing it with other medications
method: Removed OxyContin from blister packs in a narcotics cabinet and replaced it with melatonin and acetaminophen, resealed the packs, and used the stolen OxyContin for personal use; pleaded guilty to obtaining a controlled substance by misrepresentation, fraud, forgery, deception, and subterfuge.
status: Pleaded guilty on March 6, 2024; sentenced on May 24, 2024, to two years probation and a $100 special assessment; indicted by a federal grand jury in June 2023. Investigated by the FDA Office of Criminal Investigations and the DEA.

title: Maui nurse sanctioned after alleged diversion of Adderall from patient medication packet
setting: Nova Luna Inc., dba Nova Luna Center and 'Ai Pono Hawaii
method: Allegedly diverted four Adderall tablets from a patient's medication pill packet, replaced them with four Seroquel tablets, and had no authorization to possess, obtain, furnish, or administer the Adderall herself.
